what.text: Melatonin is a hormone the body makes, mainly at night, that helps run the sleep-wake cycle. Most melatonin products are made synthetically.

src.label: Melatonin: what you need to know, NIH NCCIH

what.text: Adonis does not carry topical melatonin on its own. It is part of a compounded hair-loss preparation from the Beluga catalog. We do not have a record of that product’s form, so this page does not describe it.
Using melatonin on the scalp for hair loss is off-label.

research.text: One small randomized trial and a set of open, uncontrolled studies have tested melatonin solution on the scalp.

research.title: Melatonin 0.1% scalp solution in women

facts.v: 40 women with pattern hair loss or diffuse hair loss
Share of growing (anagen) and resting (telogen) hairs on trichograms; blood melatonin

research.found: Melatonin raised the share of growing hairs at the back of the scalp in women with pattern hair loss (12 women) and at the front in women with diffuse hair loss (28 women). Other sites rose but not significantly. Blood melatonin rose but stayed below the normal night peak.

src.label: Fischer et al., Br J Dermatol, 2004

research.title: A cosmetic melatonin solution in men and women

facts.v: One drug-level study and four before-and-after studies, without placebo groups
Groups of 30, 35 and 60 people, and over 1,800 volunteers at 200 centers
Questionnaires, hair density by imaging, hair counts and hair-pull tests

research.found: The authors reported improvement in each study and good tolerance. Without placebo groups, these studies cannot show whether melatonin caused the changes.

src.label: Fischer et al., Int J Trichology, 2012

us.text: In the US, melatonin is sold as a dietary supplement. It is not an FDA-approved drug for hair loss.
NIH says melatonin is regulated as a dietary supplement in the US, under less strict rules than prescription or over-the-counter drugs.

src.label: Melatonin: what you need to know, NIH NCCIH

us.text: FDA does not approve dietary supplements before they are sold.

src.label: Questions and answers on dietary supplements, FDA

us.text: The Beluga preparation Adonis carries is compounded. Compounded drugs are not FDA approved, and this mix has not been reviewed by FDA for safety or effect.

world.lead: Melatonin is a supplement in the US but a prescription-only medicine in the UK, and the EU has authorised it as a prescription medicine for sleep. No regulator we checked has approved it for hair loss.

countries.status: Sold as a dietary supplement. Not an approved drug.

sources.label: Melatonin: what you need to know, NIH NCCIH
Questions and answers on dietary supplements, FDA

countries.status: A melatonin medicine (Slenyto) is marketed as a prescription drug. Not approved for hair loss.

sources.label: Drug Product Database status, Health Canada
Drug Product Database schedule, Health Canada

countries.status: Prescription-only medicine, authorised for certain sleep problems in adults and in children over 6. Not approved for hair loss.

sources.label: MHRA press release on undeclared melatonin, GOV.UK

countries.status: Circadin (melatonin) is authorised across the EU for short-term insomnia in people 55 and over. Prescription-only. Not approved for hair loss.
Status being confirmed with the regulator’s record.

after.title: Sport
after.text: Melatonin is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List or on the 2027 List, which takes effect January 1, 2027.

side.text: No label covers melatonin on the scalp. The side effects below are for melatonin taken by mouth.

items.text: Short-term studies in adults reported mild effects: headache, dizziness, nausea and sleepiness. Long-term effects are unclear.

src.label: Melatonin: what you need to know, NIH NCCIH

items.text: EMA lists uncommon side effects including irritability, restlessness, abnormal dreams, migraine, dizziness, sleepiness, high blood pressure, stomach pain and abnormal liver tests. It can cause drowsiness.

side.text: In the 2004 scalp trial, blood melatonin rose with treatment but stayed below the normal night peak.

src.label: Fischer et al., Br J Dermatol, 2004

unconfirmed: We have no record of the form of the Beluga product that contains melatonin, so the form is not described.
We could not open Health Canada’s natural health product records for melatonin; only the prescription drug Slenyto was confirmed.
We did not confirm whether low-dose melatonin food supplements are allowed in individual EU countries.
We could not reach Australia’s TGA (ARTG search failed), so Australia is pending.
surprises: Melatonin is sold freely as a supplement in the US, but the UK’s MHRA treats it as a prescription-only medicine and has pulled a supplement found to contain it.
Most of the hair research on topical melatonin is open studies of a cosmetic solution without placebo groups; only one small placebo-controlled trial (40 women, 2004) was found.
